lines: Meet The PM Assistant: one AI assistant for every portfolio manager. It gathers each borrower's file, drafts the routine parts of reviews, and spots trouble sooner.
You're Sam Okafor, a senior portfolio manager with twelve business borrowers. Everything here is sample data.
The Borrower File Builder checks Sam may see the borrower, then reads five sources itself, including real Federal Reserve rate data.
Every figure shows its source. Anything missing or late is listed, never filled in.
From the file, Claude drafts the routine sections of the annual review. Then code checks every number, gap and word.
Every draft is marked AI draft, and names the credit officer who decides.
The risk rating and the recommendation are left blank, for Sam to write. Nothing is submitted until Sam approves.
Every number is matched against the file. Anything it can't trace is highlighted.
Here the latest statements haven't arrived, so the draft says needs input, instead of guessing.
Coming next: early warning. Plain rules flag late statements, tight covenants, falling deposits and late payments, and Claude explains each one.
Sam decides: dismiss it with a reason, watch it, or raise it through the bank's own process.
Try to break it. Ask for a risk rating, an approval, or a price, and the guardrails stop it before any AI sees it.
Five measures from day one, with pilot portfolio managers compared against a group without it.
A pilot needs approval to use borrower data, and the higher-risk review. Our assumption, to confirm: those set the pace.
Now it's your turn. Start from Today, and run the agents live on Claude, from any screen.
